solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Leading journalists drink squash (8)

indicatorNotes.Leading: what leads comes first, so the drink is placed ahead of the journalists

annotation.surface: Senior reporters knocking back a fruit cordial.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Squash' looks like the drink, and 'drink' sits right beside it to help; but squash is the verb here, and the drink is only SUP.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to squash a revolt or a rumour is to crush it and keep it down.

entries.clue: Sewer rats seem out of place aboard ship (10)

indicatorNotes.out of place: letters that are out of place are not where they started, so RATS SEEM is rearranged
indicatorNotes.aboard: being aboard a ship means being inside it, so the jumble sits between the two letters of SS

annotation.surface: Rats that look out of place on a vessel, heading for the drains.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sewer' is read as a drain for the rats; here it is someone who sews.
annotation.definitionFit: A pun on sewer: not a drain but one who sews, and a woman who sews for a living is the classic example.

entries.clue: Audio streamed from school pitch (7)

blocks.note: a pod is a school of whales or dolphins
to pitch is to throw, or cast

annotation.surface: A recording broadcast from a school's playing field.
annotation.walkthrough: School and pitch suggest a sports field; one is a group of whales and the other a throw.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description: a programme of recorded sound delivered over the internet, audio that is streamed or downloaded.

entries.clue: Make, supply or apply plaster (6)

blocks.note: to make, as in 'the news made him speechless'
to supply or give, as in 'give assistance'
a builder's term for coating an outside wall with plaster or cement

annotation.surface: A builder's job list: make, supply, plaster.
annotation.walkthrough: In fact three definitions: 'supply' is a third meaning, not a link.
annotation.definitionFit: Three senses of one verb: to cause to be, to give or provide, and the builder's sense of coating a wall.

entries.clue: Pompous type, loaded, ill-tempered mostly (7,5)

indicatorNotes.mostly: mostly means not quite all, so SHIRTY loses its last letter

blocks.note: SHIRTY (British slang: bad-tempered) without its Y

annotation.surface: A description of a pompous, wealthy, mostly bad-tempered man.
annotation.walkthrough: Shirty is British slang for irritable or cross.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: someone puffed up with self-importance, like a shirt stuffed to look full, is a pompous type.

entries.clue: Gray’s second compendium mostly contains elegies (6)

indicatorNotes.second: the second of a word is its second letter, here the R of Gray
indicatorNotes.mostly: mostly means not quite all, so DIGEST loses its final letter
indicatorNotes.contains: a thing that contains another holds it inside, so DIGES wraps round the R

annotation.surface: Thomas Gray's second anthology is largely elegiac.
annotation.walkthrough: Gray wrote the famous 'Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard', so the surface is apt; but 'Gray's second' is just his R.
annotation.definitionFit: Near synonyms: an elegy is a mournful poem and a dirge a mournful song, both laments for the dead.

entries.clue: Nits spread by insects and ticks (8)

indicatorNotes.spread: spread means scattered about, so the letters of NITS are scattered into a new order

annotation.surface: Lice eggs carried about by insects and ticks.
annotation.walkthrough: Among nits and insects, 'ticks' looks like one more parasite; it is moments, as in 'back in a tick'.
annotation.definitionFit: Informal British usage: 'just a tick' means just a moment, so ticks are brief moments.

entries.clue: Not all reading list entries are brilliant (7)

indicatorNotes.Not all: not all of the words are used, only a run of letters from inside them

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of 'reading', through 'list', into the start of 'entries'

annotation.surface: A reviewer's grumble that some books on the reading list are poor.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is a plural verb phrase, matched by the plain verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A verb for a verb phrase: things that sparkle and shine in the light are being brilliant.

entries.clue: Large number rubbed out (4)

blocks.note: a great many, an informal word for a lot
gangster slang for killed; the old past tense of slay

annotation.surface: A big figure erased from the page.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rubbed out' suggests an eraser, but it is gangster slang for killed.
annotation.definitionFit: Two unrelated words that share a spelling: an informal word for a lot, and the past tense of slay.

entries.clue: Rider and daughter finish in a ditch almost (8)

indicatorNotes.in: D and END are put in, inside A DUM, after its D
indicatorNotes.almost: almost means not quite all, so DUMP loses its final letter

blocks.note: A + DUMP (to ditch) without its P; D END goes after its D

annotation.surface: A horse rider and his daughter nearly ending up in a ditch.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rider' pictures someone on horseback; a rider is also a clause added to a document.
annotation.definitionFit: A specialist sense: in law and politics a rider is a clause tacked on to a document, an addition at the end.

entries.clue: Aim a bit higher than the church? (6)

blocks.note: the part of a church that rises above the rest

annotation.surface: Advice to set one's sights a little above the church.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Aim a bit higher' reads as advice, but the wordplay is a cryptic hint for the part of a church that rises above the rest.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to aim high and to set one's hopes on something are the same ambition.

entries.clue: At sea each lounge is somewhere to relax (6,6)

indicatorNotes.At sea: to be at sea is to be confused, so the letters are jumbled

annotation.surface: On a cruise ship, every lounge is a place to unwind.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Is' belongs to the fodder, not a link, which is easy to miss.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description: a long reclining chair is literally a place to put one's feet up.

entries.clue: Latest report by old newspaper character (5-2-3-3)

annotation.surface: The latest dispatch from a figure at an old newspaper.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Newspaper character' suggests a cartoon figure or columnist, but the paper and the character are separate pieces, and character here means courage or spirit.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: the state of the art is the current peak of a technology, so anything described this way is the latest.

entries.clue: Welfare checks statesmen forced on society (5,5)

indicatorNotes.forced: something forced is bent out of its natural shape, so the letters are wrenched into a new order

blocks.note: S = society, added on to the fodder

annotation.surface: Politicians imposing benefit checks on the public.
annotation.walkthrough: The anagram takes in STATESMEN and the S together.
annotation.definitionFit: A British term: benefits are granted only after checking a claimant's income and savings, their means.

entries.clue: Hotel auditor’s legal documents (4)

indicatorNotes.auditor’s: an auditor is literally a hearer, so the answer is what a listener hears

annotation.surface: An accountant at a hotel with legal papers.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Auditor' pictures an accountant; here it simply means a listener.
annotation.definitionFit: A proper name standing for the thing: the Ritz is a famous luxury hotel in London.

entries.clue: Hand stopping a ball going in (10)

indicatorNotes.stopping: a thing stopping a gap plugs it, so MITT sits inside A DANCE like a cork in a bottle

annotation.surface: A goalkeeper's hand keeping out a ball heading into the net.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is football; 'ball' is a formal dance, not the thing being kicked.
annotation.definitionFit: A formal synonym: being allowed to enter a place is gaining entry, the act of going in.

entries.clue: Golf club contracted with another in China (8)

indicatorNotes.contracted: a contracted word is shortened, so WEDGE loses its last letter

blocks.note: WEDGE, a golf club, without its E
a wood is another kind of golf club

annotation.surface: A golfer in China signing up with a club.
annotation.walkthrough: 'China' reads as the country, but it is porcelain.
annotation.definitionFit: A brand name for the thing: an English pottery firm famous for its fine china.

entries.clue: Book about Hearts initially exaggerated their goal tally (10)

indicatorNotes.about: about means around, so SHE is placed around CORES
indicatorNotes.initially: initially means at the start, so each of the last two words gives its first letter

blocks.note: She, the novel by H. Rider Haggard

annotation.surface: A book about Heart of Midlothian football club inflating its goal count.
annotation.walkthrough: Hearts is a Scottish football club, which is the picture; here it is just CORES. 'Their' looks like part of the definition but supplies its T.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by function: the sheet a scorer fills in during a match is where a team's goals are totted up.

entries.clue: Cop turned killer in LA? (7)

blocks.note: milk that has turned has gone off
American slang: to ice someone is to kill them

annotation.surface: A Los Angeles policeman who became a murderer.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the slang: ICER is a killer only in US gangster talk, hence 'in LA'.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: cop is the informal word for a police officer.

entries.clue: Italy’s capital missing from simple map (4)

indicatorNotes.capital: a word's capital letter is its first, so Italy gives I
indicatorNotes.missing from: something missing from a word has been taken out of it, so PLAIN loses its I

annotation.surface: Rome is missing from a basic map.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Italy's capital' wants to be Rome; it is only the letter I.
annotation.definitionFit: Near synonym: a street layout or floor layout drawn from above is a kind of map.

entries.clue: Falling behind insulation (7)

blocks.note: material wrapped round pipes and tanks to keep the heat in

annotation.surface: Falling behind with the insulation work.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Behind insulation' reads as a location, but the clue splits after 'behind'.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: the verb form of trailing behind, and the plumbing noun for pipe wrapping.

entries.clue: Note that’s upset a Cheshire constituent (6)

indicatorNotes.upset: to upset something is to tip it over, and in a down entry that turns the word upside down

blocks.note: a tenner is a ten-pound note

annotation.surface: A letter that has offended a voter in Cheshire.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Constituent' pictures a voter in a Cheshire constituency; Cheshire is a cheese.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Cheshire is a British cheese, and this enzyme that curdles milk is one of its ingredients.

entries.clue: Climber’s knot — guess if he got tangled (6,2,5)

indicatorNotes.tangled: tangled rope is twisted out of order, so the letters are twisted into a new one

annotation.surface: Wondering which knot a climber used, if he got his rope in a tangle.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Guess' looks like anagram fodder beside 'tangled'; it is FIGURE, and only IF HE GOT is rearranged.
annotation.definitionFit: A specialist term: climbers tie this knot, shaped like the numeral 8, to fasten the rope to a harness.

entries.clue: Help to lower a pulse (4)

indicatorNotes.to lower: to lower something is to move it down, and in a down entry the A moves down the word

blocks.note: the letter A that moves down

annotation.surface: Aiding a heartbeat to slow down.
annotation.walkthrough: Only one letter moves: the A of ABET is taken down to third place.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: the pulse is the regular throb of the heart, each throb one unit of it.

entries.clue: Key bank bond held by a third party (6)

annotation.definition: bond held by a third party

blocks.note: the Escape key on a keyboard
a bank of seats or switches is a row

annotation.surface: A financial key: a bank bond looked after by someone else.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bank' reads as the financial kind, but it is a row, as in a bank of lights.
annotation.definitionFit: A legal term: money or a deed lodged with a neutral party until a deal's conditions are met.

entries.clue: Mature, since working for model employers (8)

indicatorNotes.working: something working is in motion, so the letters are set moving into a new order

annotation.surface: Grown-up since taking a job with exemplary employers.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Model employers' reads as ideal bosses; it means firms that hire out fashion models.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: firms that sign and book fashion models are the models' employers.

entries.clue: Lecture dealing with India partitioning (6)

indicatorNotes.partitioning: to partition something is to divide it, so the I is set inside TRADE and splits it in two

blocks.note: I = India in the phonetic alphabet, placed after T

annotation.surface: A talk on trade relations during the partition of India.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface recalls the 1947 Partition; here 'partitioning' just means I splits TRADE.
annotation.definitionFit: Near synonym: a long angry harangue is a telling-off lecture.

entries.clue: Firstly, scout acquires inside info about reserves (4,4)

indicatorNotes.Firstly: firstly means first of all, so scout gives only its first letter
indicatorNotes.inside: acquires goes inside the info, so GETS sits within GEN
indicatorNotes.about: about means turned around, so the assembled letters are read backwards

annotation.surface: A talent scout gets inside information on the reserve players.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Inside info' looks like one phrase, but 'inside' is the container signal; the whole string is then turned round.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: money put aside for the future, a financial reserve.
